name: Post Type Information
author: GrandSlambert

sections.description:
Post Type Information adds the custom content you choose to the Dashboard At a Glance box. Each row shows a count and links to the matching admin screen.

Features

  • Choose which custom post types and custom taxonomies appear, on a settings page.
  • Shows the published count for each selected post type and links to its list table.
  • Shows the term count for each selected taxonomy and links to its term screen.
  • Skips built-in posts, pages, categories, and tags. Those are already in At a Glance.
  • Hides a row when the current user cannot edit that post type or manage that taxonomy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the post-type-information folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install through Plugins > Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Settings > Post Type Information and choose which post types and taxonomies to display.
  4. Open the Dashboard. The selected items appear in At a Glance.
sections.faq:
How do I choose what shows in At a Glance?

Go to Settings > Post Type Information. Check the custom post types and custom taxonomies you want. Save the settings, then reload the Dashboard.

Nothing is added until you select it. Built-in types such as posts and pages, and built-in taxonomies such as categories and tags, are not in the lists because WordPress already shows them.

What does each row show?

A post type row shows the number of published items and the post type label. The link opens that type’s list table (edit.php for that post type).

A taxonomy row shows how many terms exist, including empty terms, and the taxonomy label. The link opens the term screen for that taxonomy.

The label is singular when the count is 1 and plural otherwise.

Why is a type I selected missing from the Dashboard?

The row is shown only if your user can edit that post type, or manage terms for that taxonomy. Another user with a different role may see a different set of rows.

If the post type or taxonomy is no longer registered, it is skipped.

Does uninstall remove the settings?

Yes. Deleting the plugin removes the saved post type and taxonomy selections.

Where can I get support?

https://wordpress.org/support/plugin/post-type-information/
